paper_summary: PhD dissertation (M. K. John, LSU 2009) on a shape-memory-polymer (SMP, styrene-based Veriflex thermoset, Tg 62 C) syntactic foam made with 40 vol% Q-Cel 6014 glass microballoons, with and without 0.15 vol% multi-walled carbon nanotubes. The foam was characterised by DSC, TEM, flash thermal conductivity and flat-wise uniaxial compression (ASTM C365), and a four-phase/three-phase micromechanics sphere model was used to back out the elastic constants of the equivalent SMP layer and of the foam. The foam was then used as the core of a VARIM-made glass-fabric-skinned sandwich and of an orthogrid-stiffened sandwich, which were thermomechanically programmed, impacted repeatedly at 30 J and 53 J, healed by confined shape recovery and tested in compression-after-impact; healing efficiencies of 100% or more were obtained over 7 impact-healing cycles.

extraction_notes:
Unit conversions: moduli given in GPa converted to MPa (1.24 GPa -> 1240 MPa; Table 2 foam E = 0.27 GPa -> 270 MPa). Microballoon volume fraction 40% -> 0.40; MWCNT 0.15 vol% recorded in additional_fillers. Radius ratio eta = a/b = 41.69/42.5 = 0.981 (stated inner/outer radii, wall thickness 0.81 um). Compression strain rate 1.73e-3 1/s derived from the stated 1.3 mm/min cross-head rate and the stated 12.5 mm specimen thickness; for the CAI (sandwich) tests the gauge length is not stated so strain rate is left null.

Two distinct foams are reported and are kept separate: (a) smart foam WITH 0.15 vol% MWCNT, cured 75/90/100 C (Ch. 2 and Ch. 4, compressive yield 5.91 MPa regularly cured); (b) smart foam WITHOUT nanotubes, cured 79.4/107.2/121.1 C (Ch. 5, Table 6, compressive yield 20.22 MPa regularly cured). The much higher strength of (b) is consistent with the text ('the one without carbon nanotubes has a considerably higher yield strength and modulus of elasticity').

The modulus 270 MPa attached to foam (a) comes from Table 2, where the text states K0 'is the modulus of the equivalent smart syntactic foam obtained from uniaxial compression tests'; it is therefore treated as a measured foam modulus rather than a purely modelled value, but confidence is lowered accordingly. The other Table 2 rows (equivalent solid glass microballoon E = 1.94 GPa, equivalent SMP layer E = 0.15 GPa) are phase properties from the micromechanics model, not composite properties, so no records were created for them.

Records whose sample_label starts with 'Smart-foam-cored sandwich' or 'Orthogrid-stiffened' are SANDWICH PANELS (syntactic-foam core plus glass-fabric skins, and in Ch. 5 a glass-fibre orthogrid skeleton), not bare foam; this is flagged in every specimen_notes field so they can be filtered out of foam-only analyses. Their compression-after-impact values are structural, not intrinsic foam properties.

Values deliberately NOT extracted: (1) low-velocity-impact results (Tables 3-5 and Figs 24, 35, 37: deflection at peak load, maximum load in kN, initiation/propagation/total energy in J) have no corresponding schema field - energy in J cannot be converted to MJ/m^3 without the deformed volume, which is not given. (2) CAI yield strengths quoted only as percentages of the control (1st impact 83.9%, 7th impact 94.9% of 12.23 MPa) are left null rather than back-calculated. (3) Literature values in the Chapter 1 review are class-level ranges without a stated composition or matrix - 'uniaxial compression strengths up to 100 MPa, hydrostatic compression strengths up to 150 MPa, uniaxial tension strengths up to 25~30 MPa and tensile Young's modulus up to 2500~3000 MPa' (Luxmoore & Owen [7]) and 'Young's modulus increased linearly from 2 to 2.47 GPa' (Kishore et al. [9]) - so no secondary records could be built with a valid matrix_class or filler loading. The only secondary record kept is the manufacturer datasheet for the neat Veriflex SMP matrix. (4) Densities of the foams were never reported; specific heat capacities (1395.6 and 1364.5 J/kg.K) have no schema field and are recorded in specimen_notes. (5) Figures 15, 16, 26, 44, 46 were not read off the plots; only values stated in the text or tables were used.
